newsitem.title: UK: UK insurer Norwich Union plans flotation.
newsitem.headline: UK insurer Norwich Union plans flotation.

text.p: Britain's Norwich Union Life Insurance Society said on Wednesday it plans to float on the London Stock Exchange, creating a new holding company Norwich Union Plc.

The float, expected to raise some 4.5 billion pounds, will be the first conversion of a British mutual life insurer into a public company. Norwich Union is one of the country's largest insurance groups with funds under management of about 40 billion pounds and worldwide gross premium income of 4.7 billion.
Qualifying members will receive free shares in Norwich Union Plc and preferential rights to subscribe cash for further shares but the door for new members will be closed from today, it said.

The Norwich has more than five million customers worldwide of which about three million are members of the society. Most holders of existing life, pensions and annuity policies of the society are members, which includes holders of policies issued by its overseas operations. The group earned around 28 percent of its 1995 gross written premiums outside Britain.
Norwich said the flotation will allow its general insurance business to be transferred out of the life fund thereby removing some policyholders to these volatile businesses.
It will also put a higher value on its life operations and improve the companies access to funds on the capital markets.
